stem: Batch X reports 90% rooting at day 14 and Batch Y reports 78% at day 7. Why is a direct performance ranking weak?
choices: Rank Batch X higher because 90% is a better rooting outcome than 78%, even though the observations were taken on different days.
Rank by cultivar history instead because rooting percentages from different observation days cannot be interpreted quantitatively.
Avoid direct ranking until the batches are compared at the same defined endpoint or with an explicitly validated time-to-root metric.
Treat the observation day as unimportant if both batches used the same propagation protocol and environment.
rationale: Rooting success changes over time. A 90% result at day 14 and a 78% result at day 7 are not equivalent endpoints, so a direct performance ranking confounds success rate with time allowed to root. The batches should be compared at a common validated endpoint or with a metric that explicitly incorporates rooting time.
